quote.text: In every walk with nature, one receives far more than he seeks.
quote.author: John Muir

fun_fact.text: Hummingbirds are the only birds that can fly backwards! Their wings rotate in a full circle, allowing them to hover in place and zip in any direction. A hummingbird's heart beats up to 1,200 times per minute during flight.

short_read.title: The Secret Lives of Garden Snails
short_read.teaser: These tiny mollusks can sleep for up to three years and have thousands of teeth arranged on a tongue-like ribbon. Discover the surprisingly fascinating world right under your garden leaves.

medium_read.title: Budapest's Thermal Baths: A Journey Through History
medium_read.teaser: Hungary's capital is built on over 100 thermal springs that have been enjoyed since Roman times. Explore the beautiful architecture and healing traditions of these iconic Hungarian gathering places.

long_read.title: The Return of Sea Otters to the Pacific Northwest
long_read.teaser: Once hunted nearly to extinction, sea otters are slowly making a comeback along the Olympic Coast. This is the story of their recovery and the critical role they play in keeping kelp forests healthy.

port_angeles.title: Wildlife Watching at Dungeness Spit
port_angeles.description: August is prime time for spotting black-tailed deer at Dungeness National Wildlife Refuge, just east of Port Angeles. The 5.5-mile sand spit is also home to over 250 species of birds, harbor seals, and stunning views of the Strait. Early morning walks offer the best wildlife viewing opportunities.

puzzle_1.question: A hummingbird can beat its wings about ___ times per second.
puzzle_1.correct_response: Exactly right! Those tiny wings are a blur of motion — no wonder they hum!
puzzle_1.close_response: Very close! Hummingbird wings beat about 80 times per second — almost too fast to see!
puzzle_1.wrong_response: Hummingbird wings beat about 80 times per second — that's nearly 5,000 beats per minute! Amazing little creatures.
puzzle_1.learn_more_text: Different hummingbird species have different wing speeds. The Giant Hummingbird beats its wings only 10-15 times per second, while the tiny Amethyst Woodstar can reach 100 beats per second!

puzzle_2.question: Which Hungarian word means 'thank you'?
puzzle_2.correct_response: Köszönöm! You got it right — that's wonderful!
puzzle_2.wrong_response: The word is 'köszönöm' (or the shorter 'köszi'). 'Szia' means hello, 'igen' means yes, and 'viszlát' means goodbye!
puzzle_2.learn_more_text: Hungarian is unique among European languages — it's part of the Finno-Ugric language family, more closely related to Finnish and Estonian than to neighboring German, Slovak, or Romanian.

puzzle_3.question: What animal is known as the 'gardener of the forest' because it buries acorns that grow into oak trees?
puzzle_3.correct_response: Yes! Blue jays cache thousands of acorns each fall and forget many of them, planting future oak forests. They're nature's gardeners!
puzzle_3.wrong_response: It's the blue jay! These clever birds hide thousands of acorns for winter but forget where many are buried, inadvertently planting oak trees across the landscape.
puzzle_3.learn_more_text: A single blue jay can carry up to five acorns at once — three in its crop, one in its mouth, and one in the tip of its bill. They can transport acorns up to 2.5 miles from the parent tree.
